svg.title: How an update of an engine reaches the repositories
svg.desc: Renovate opens a pull request for each engine, a week after the release of its new version, a minor or major one too. Its required checks, engine contracts among them, run the engine without a key; when one fails, the update doesn't merge, and no other engine waits for it. When they pass, the update merges on its own. The push to main starts the Canary, which runs the AI's whole path with the engine's action and its secret, and the release bot updates its pull request. That pull request's required check, the Canary of main, waits while a Canary of main runs. When the latest one passed, the release merges and reaches every repository that uses the action. When it failed, the release waits, the bot-health bot opens an issue, and a revert of the update or another run of the Canary lets the release go.
